can_support: the task's registration: it exists, it is enabled, its action is the declared interpreter and script, and it repeats every fifteen minutes
the most recent run, as the scheduler itself records it, sampled as often as the witness runs
a live launch, from the process table: a tick whose parent is the Task Scheduler service was launched by the schema, not by a person
cannot_support: an absence of execution inside any slot of this period: no external source covers those hours, so a slot with no internal event is UNKNOWN, not proven unattended
a distinction between a time-trigger launch and an engine launch asked for by hand: both are started by the Task Scheduler service and neither leaves an event here
a per-run exit status: only the most recent result is readable, and only while it is the most recent
per_run_external_evidence.correlation_rule: a per-run record has to be correlated by the task's full name, its own instance and its action, with the timestamps of the start and of the action's start and finish; LastTaskResult and LastRunTime alone are the most recent values of a task, not a history, and an event id on its own — 100 against 110, a scheduled trigger against a launch asked for by hand — does not establish that the run was scheduled
per_run_external_evidence.event_ids_reading: the provider declares these per-run events, but this installation holds none of them: the semantics could not be verified event by event here, and no claim about any particular run is derived from an id alone

per_run_external_evidence.reason: Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational is disabled on this host and no event file exists for it, so the channel has never recorded a single run of this task; the enabled Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Maintenance channel holds only its own maintenance events, which name no task; and the Security channel, which would carry a process-creation record if that audit subcategory were enabled and if this session could read it, is not readable here

remediation.what: enable the Task Scheduler operational channel for this host
remediation.what_it_would_give: per-run events (100 started, 102 completed, 107/110 triggered, 200/201 action started and finished) with their own record ids, so every slot could be corroborated run by run instead of from a point-in-time sample
remediation.why_not_applied: it changes a machine-wide audit setting, it needs an administrator, and it cannot recover the runs that have already happened: the channel records from the moment it is enabled

rotation_assessment.does_not_authorise: clearing, resizing, re-enabling or pruning any log: this reading is taken read-only and the loss it names cannot be repaired for the instants that have already passed
rotation_assessment.reading: where a log is circular and has filled, its oldest records are already gone: the number of the oldest record still present is the count of what this host can no longer answer for. A channel that cannot be read at all is kept apart from one that never recorded and from an empty log — only a readable, empty channel could support the reading that it holds no run. Either way the loss is a property of the evidence, recorded so that a slot the surviving record does not cover is never called provably unattended

scheduler_reporting_now.reading: the last run instant and the last result are the scheduler's own record of the task; they are the strongest external evidence this host can give, and they describe only the most recent run
